meta.title: Solid Share — Files, contacts and passes on a pod you own
meta.description: Solid Share is an open-source Android app for your Solid pod. Browse files, keep contacts and passes, share them by WebID, link or QR code, and let other apps reach your pod on terms you set. No servers, no accounts, no tracking.
meta.ogdescription: Files, contacts and passes on your own Solid pod, shared on your terms. Free software for Android.

on a pod you own
hero.3: Solid Share turns your Solid pod into a personal data wallet on Android. The app has no server of its own. It talks to your pod directly, so nothing you store passes through us.
hero.4: Android 8.0 and later · The F-Droid build links no proprietary dependency · APK on GitHub

page.aria1: What Solid Share does not do
new.3: Solid Share is now the host app for Solid on Android: another app asks it, instead of asking you for a password. The app also speaks four more languages, opens your files without handing them to another app, and answers on Home with what changed while you were away.
new.5: Apps, on your terms Other apps reach your pod through Solid Share. You scope what each one may do, and a new Apps tab takes it back.
new.6: Five languages German, Spanish, French and Italian join English. The app follows your phone, or the language you pick.
new.7: A new Home Your inbox, the files you opened or that changed, what you shared, and your next pass, on one screen.
new.8: Files that open in place Images, PDFs and text open inside the app, and any app can share a file straight into your pod.
new.9: Inrupt pods fixed Share notifications and access requests now arrive on an Inrupt account.
how.2: Three steps, and your pod stays yours
how.3: Solid is an open web standard for personal data stores, called pods. You pick the provider, or you run your own server.
how.5: Use Inrupt, Solid Community, Data Pod, or any custom OIDC issuer URL. You can log into several pods at once and switch between them.
how.7: The app authenticates directly with the provider you picked. From then on it reads and writes resources on your pod, from your phone.
how.9: Grant a specific WebID, or anyone with the link, View, Add or Edit access. Widen, narrow or revoke the share at any time.

cards.1: What changed while you were away
cards.2: Home opens on the things waiting for you: unread notifications and access requests, the files you opened or that changed, what you shared, and your next pass. It reads what is already on the device, so it opens at once and works offline.
cards.4: Everything you have seen is on the device, in an encrypted database, and opens with no connection. Every write queues and drains by itself when the connection comes back.
cards.6: Log into more than one pod and switch between them. An expired session is a state, not a logout — reconnect in one tap and keep your data in place.
cards.8: The recipient is told when their access changes. Access requests arrive as notifications you can accept or decline.
cards.10: English, German, Spanish, French and Italian. The app follows your phone language, and you can pick a different one for Solid Share alone.
cards.12: Solid Protocol, Solid-OIDC, Web Access Control with an ACP fallback, and vCard. Your data stays readable by any other Solid client.
cards.14: Write a Solid app for Android and let Solid Share hold the accounts and the tokens. The Android Solid Services SDK gives your app the pod, the consent screen and the access checks.
privacy.2: Two builds. You choose what runs.
privacy.3: Solid Share has no database of its own. Your files, contacts, tickets and shares live on the pod you chose, under your own identity. Other apps that ask through Solid Share receive the results of a pod call, never a credential they could reuse, and what you allowed each one stays on this device — it is never written to your pod.
privacy.7: No crash reporting, no usage events
privacy.8: Built from the public source tree
privacy.12: Sends crash reports and basic usage events to Google (Firebase)
privacy.13: No advertising ID, no cross-app tracking, no profiling
faq.3: Do I need a Solid pod before I install the app?
faq.4: Yes — your data lives on a pod. The login screen lists public providers such as Inrupt, Solid Community and Data Pod, and accepts any custom OIDC issuer URL, including a server you run yourself. A pod at a public provider is created in a few minutes. Learn about Solid pods.
faq.6: Nothing. The app is free software under the MIT licence, with no ads and no paid tiers. Pod storage comes from the provider you pick — several offer free space, and a self-hosted server costs only the hardware it runs on.
faq.7: Which Android versions does it run on?
faq.8: Android 8.0 and later. The app is on Google Play and on F-Droid, and the APK is on GitHub.
faq.9: What is different between the F-Droid and Google Play builds?
faq.10: The features are identical. The F-Droid and GitHub build contains no analytics code at all. The Google Play build adds Firebase crash reporting. The privacy policy describes both in full.
faq.11: Can other apps on my phone use my pod?
faq.12: Yes, and only as far as you let them. A Solid app built on the Android Solid Services SDK asks Solid Share instead of asking you for a password, so your credentials never leave this app. The first time one asks, Solid Share shows you which account it wants, what it wants to do and where. Nothing reaches your pod until you allow it, the Apps tab lists everything you have allowed, and removing an app takes effect on its next call. If you write Solid apps yourself, the Android Solid Services SDK is how your app asks.
faq.13: Which languages does the app speak?
faq.14: English, German, Spanish, French and Italian, on every screen. The app starts in your phone's language when it is one of the five, and in English otherwise. A Language row on your Profile changes it at any time, for Solid Share alone.
faq.16: Yes. Everything you have seen is kept on the device in an encrypted database and opens with no connection. Writes queue and sync by themselves when the connection returns, and you can pin a file to keep its content available offline.
faq.17: Where do I report a bug or ask for a feature?
faq.18: Open an issue on GitHub, or reach me through my contact page.
